vibe: Patch-now warnings dominate the morning as actively exploited enterprise flaws pile up, while AI agents are becoming both a security threat and a serious new layer of cloud infrastructure.

cyber.title: CISA warns of Sharepoint, WSO2, Adobe Commerce flaws exploited in attacks
cyber.summary: CISA added four actively exploited flaws to KEV: WSO2 CVE-2026-5430, Adobe Commerce/Magento CVE-2026-71362, SharePoint CVE-2026-65660 and MikroTik RouterOS CVE-2026-67279. Patch or isolate exposed systems now.

cyber.title: Kiteworks urges customers to shut down their servers amid ‘imminent’ threat of cyberattack
cyber.summary: Kiteworks has urged customers to shut down affected servers because of an imminent attack risk. This is an unusually strong vendor warning: identify exposed deployments, follow the shutdown guidance and preserve logs.

cyber.title: Roundcube Pre-Auth SQL Injection Flaw Actively Exploited in the Wild
cyber.summary: A pre-authentication SQL-injection flaw in Roundcube is being exploited. Internet-facing webmail needs urgent patching and a review for suspicious requests, sessions and database activity.

cyber.title: Compromised GitHub Actions Came Back Online and Resumed Executing Mini Shai-Hulud Malware
cyber.summary: Previously compromised GitHub Actions returned and resumed executing Mini Shai-Hulud malware. Audit workflow dependencies, pin actions to trusted commits and rotate secrets where affected workflows ran.

cyber.title: Cloudflare Fixes Flaw That Let One Container Read Another Customer's Leftover Disk Data
cyber.summary: Cloudflare fixed a container-isolation failure that exposed residual disk data from other customers. The incident is a sharp reminder to encrypt sensitive data and not assume ephemeral multi-tenant storage is clean.

cyber.title: 'Salesbleed' Exploits Salesforce Agents to Enable Slack Phishing
cyber.summary: Salesbleed abuses Salesforce agents as a route into convincing Slack phishing. Agent integrations should be treated as privileged identities, with narrow scopes, strong approval boundaries and monitored cross-app actions.

cyber.title: Crook used three open source agents to break into a Fortune 500 hospitality company, a major US airline and 25+ other orgs
cyber.summary: A criminal reportedly chained three open-source agents to compromise more than 25 organisations, including a major airline and hospitality company. The barrier to scalable intrusion automation is dropping fast.

cyber.title: MacSync malware uses public iCloud calendars to deliver new payloads
cyber.summary: MacSync is using public iCloud calendars as a command-and-control delivery path. Defenders should look beyond conventional domains and inspect unusual Calendar access and payload activity on Macs.

cyber.title: Kothamine malware uses Tailscale’s tailcat to evade network detection
cyber.summary: Kothamine abuses Tailscale's tailcat tooling to blend command traffic into legitimate encrypted overlay networking. Review unexpected Tailscale binaries, identities and device enrolments.

cyber.title: Doubts grow over claims OpenAI agent hacked Australian Medicare portal
cyber.summary: Follow-up reporting challenges the government's initial characterisation of the Medicare portal incident. The breach remains important, but attribution to an autonomous OpenAI agent is less certain than yesterday's headlines suggested.

cyber.title: Another week, another data breach for Revolut customers
cyber.summary: Revolut is dealing with another customer-data exposure. Details are still emerging, but the repeat incident warrants watching for notifications, credential abuse and targeted phishing.

ai.title: For months, OpenAI’s agent swarms have been attacking online databases to find obscure facts
ai.summary: OpenAI has been running large swarms of agents against online databases to retrieve obscure facts. It shows agent scaling moving from demos into aggressive real-world information gathering, with obvious load and access-control implications.

ai.title: Anthropic to pay Akamai $11.6 billion over seven years in cloud deal
ai.summary: Anthropic's reported $11.6 billion, seven-year Akamai deal is a major diversification of AI infrastructure beyond the hyperscalers and a strong signal that inference capacity is becoming strategic.

ai.title: U.S. appeals court upholds designation of Anthropic as supply chain risk
ai.summary: A US appeals court upheld the Pentagon's designation of Anthropic as a supply-chain risk. The ruling could materially affect government procurement and the wider enterprise trust debate around frontier models.

ai.title: The cheap new AI model taking aim at OpenAI and Anthropic
ai.summary: A lower-cost model is challenging the frontier incumbents on price and capability. Worth watching as inference economics, not just benchmark leadership, increasingly decide enterprise adoption.

ai.title: Ollaya – Ollama for open-source, Jev-style decision models
ai.summary: Ollaya brings an Ollama-like local workflow to open decision models. Strong Hacker News interest makes it a practical experiment for private, CPU-friendly classification and routing workloads.

ai.title: On Anthropic’s AI Misuse Report
ai.summary: Bruce Schneier examines Anthropic's latest misuse report, including espionage, AI supply-chain targeting and attackers using model capabilities as infrastructure. Useful sober context beyond vendor headlines.

ai.title: OpenAI is preparing a $500 ChatGPT Pro Max plan with faster Codex
ai.summary: OpenAI is reportedly preparing a $500-a-month tier offering faster Codex access. Treat the details as provisional, but it points to premium pricing for scarce agentic-compute capacity.

it.title: Dutch governments builds alternative for Microsoft based on NixOS
it.summary: Dutch public-sector teams are building a NixOS-based alternative to Microsoft-centric desktop infrastructure. The project drew exceptional developer interest and is a serious digital-sovereignty case study.

it.title: Asahi fork embraces LLMs and lands Linux on the M4 Mac mini
it.summary: An Asahi Linux fork has brought Linux to the M4 Mac mini while using LLM-assisted development. Interesting both as hardware enablement and as a test of AI-assisted low-level systems work.

it.title: Platform-independent SIMD in Go
it.summary: Go is experimenting with portable SIMD, which could unlock major performance gains without architecture-specific code. This is highly relevant to systems and cloud workloads doing vector-heavy processing.

it.title: 2026 just became the year of FreeBSD on the (Amazonian cloud) desktop
it.summary: FreeBSD is gaining a practical cloud-desktop path on AWS. It is niche, but useful for teams wanting a managed remote environment around BSD tooling and workloads.

videos.title: New frontier AI models, TypeSafe’s Jev AI, & NASA’s IBM collab
videos.verdict: WATCH — a substantive panel on why model names matter less than tool use, long-running reliability, efficiency and infrastructure cost.
videos.summary: IBM's panel argues that frontier-model evaluation is shifting from raw benchmark gains toward sustained work, reliable tool use and cost. It also covers open decision models and IBM/NASA collaboration; the middle discussion is the strongest segment.

videos.title: Meta is pivoting again... everything you missed from Connect 2026
videos.verdict: WATCH — a fast, sceptical ten-minute catch-up on Meta's Muse strategy and new AI hardware.
videos.summary: Fireship compresses Meta Connect into the key shift: Muse is becoming a persistent personal agent spanning glasses, desktop, email and a Tamagotchi-like device. Funny, dense and useful if you skipped the keynote.

videos.title: New Way Now: Customer Zero: How Google Cloud Consulting accelerates agentic AI
videos.verdict: SKIM — useful customer-zero lessons, though it is polished Google marketing.
videos.summary: Google Cloud Consulting describes using its own organisation as the first customer for agentic workflows, with product teams and consultants iterating before external rollout. The practical value is in the adoption and feedback-loop framing.

videos.title: New Way Now: Deutsche Telekom cuts SAP energy use 40% with Google Cloud
videos.verdict: SKIM — a compact cloud-modernisation case study with a concrete efficiency result.
videos.summary: Deutsche Telekom says moving a large legacy SAP estate to Google Cloud cut energy use by about 40%. It is vendor-produced, but the scale and migration outcome make it relevant to cloud engineers.
